newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Bank Queensland to get new directors.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Bank Queensland to get new directors.

text.p: The Queensland state government, which holds a 44 percent stake in the Bank of Queensland Ltd, said on Wednesday it will replace three retiring bank directors with its own appointees at the bank's annual meeting next month.
The new directors will be government nominees Daryl McDonough, Neil Summerson and Don Harvey, a spokesman for deputy premier and State Treasurer, Joan Sheldon, said.
The government last month announced it would move to have its own directors nominated for board appointments to the Bank of Queensland, aimed at replacing three bank directors.

However, the three bank directors, Graham Tucker, Ted Ranson and Bernard Rowley announced their retirement from the bank board late on Tuesday. Bank of Queensland chairman Neil Roberts announced yesterday that Tucker, former chairman of Suncorp and fellow Suncorp director Ted Ranson would retire from the board at the conclusion of the bank's annual meeting on December 5.
With the merger of Suncorp, Metway Bank Ltd and Queensland Industry Development Corp (QIDC) occurring on December 1, Rowley was retiring as of November 30, Roberts said in a statement.
Roberts, who has distanced his bank from the merger plan, recently told Reuters an offer to buy back 30 percent of the bank's capital from the government at current market prices, was still current.
